title: Vacancy-Driven Gelation Using Defect-Rich Nanoassemblies of 2D Transition Metal Dichalcogenides and Polymeric Binder for Biomedical Applications

notes: Two branches after the crosslink claim: gelation -> in-medium gelation -> cell encapsulation, and stiffness. Information lost: CV active-centre densities (Fig S2), defect-ratio gelation kinetics (Fig S4), cyclic compression recovery (S7), zeta potential. Audits: o11 (overall Raman attenuation undercuts thiol-band disappearance), o14 (gel Mo 3d fit components are not valid spin-orbit doublets; 235.3 eV matches Mo6+), o19 (F2d shows no 3 kPa plateau within 4 h). XPS Delta=3.15 eV cited for 2H phase is the fixed Mo 3d spin-orbit splitting and does not discriminate phases (not added as audit: s2 is off-spine).
